items.title: Section: Marks Twenty-Five Through Thirty-Two — A Lion's Own Jaw, a Voice Like Thunder, and the Crown None Can See

items.zh: 二十五者、頷如師子。二十六者、其舌廣薄，若從口出，普覆面輪及髮邊際。二十七者、於諸味中得最上味。二十八者、得大梵音，言詞哀雅能悅眾意，譬若羯羅頻迦之音，其聲雷震猶如天鼓。二十九者、其目紺青。三十者、睫如牛王。三十一者、其頂上現烏瑟膩沙。三十二者、眉間毫相其色光白，螺文右旋，是大丈夫大丈夫相。
items.en: Twenty-fifth, a jaw full as a lion's own. Twenty-sixth, a tongue broad and thin, able, when extended, to cover the face up to the hairline. Twenty-seventh, obtaining the finest of every flavour. Twenty-eighth, a great, resonant voice, its words moving and elegant, delighting the mind of all who hear, like the kalaviṅka bird's own song, its sound thunderous like a heavenly drum. Twenty-ninth, eyes of deep blue-black. Thirtieth, eyelashes like a bull-king's own. Thirty-first, a raised protrusion appearing atop the head. Thirty-second, a tuft of hair between the eyebrows, radiant white, curling to the right — this is the great being's own mark among great beings.

items.title: Section: Eighty Exemplary Signs Open — Sixty Below the Neck, From Perfect Fingernails to a Straight, Unbending Spine

items.zh: 云何如來八十隨好？謂兩手足具二十指及以節爪、並皆殊妙，是即名為二十隨好。兩手、兩足表裏八處，手四、足四並皆殊妙，是即名為八種隨好。兩踝、膝、股六處殊妙，是即名為六種隨好。兩臂、肘、腕六處殊妙，是即名為六種隨好。腰、縫殊妙，各一隨好。兩核殊妙，為二隨好。陰藏殊妙，為一隨好。兩臀殊妙，為二隨好。臗、臚、臍三並皆殊妙，各一隨好。兩脇、腋、乳並皆殊妙，為六隨好。腹、胸、項、脊，各一隨好。如是所說，除頸已上，於下身分六十隨好。
items.en:
Second, the eighty exemplary signs; first, posing the question. What are the Tathāgata's own eighty exemplary signs?
Second, listing them; first, the sixty exemplary signs found below the neck. Both hands and feet, complete with twenty fingers and toes together with their joints and nails, all wondrously excellent — this is called twenty exemplary signs. The eight surfaces, front and back, of both hands and both feet — four of the hands, four of the feet — all wondrously excellent — this is called eight exemplary signs. Both ankles, knees, and thighs, six places wondrously excellent — this is called six exemplary signs. Both upper arms, elbows, and wrists, six places wondrously excellent — this is called six exemplary signs. The waist and the natural seam, each wondrously excellent, one sign each. Both cores, wondrously excellent, two signs. The concealed organ, wondrously excellent, one sign. Both buttocks, wondrously excellent, two signs. The hips, abdomen, and navel, all wondrously excellent, one sign each. Both sides, armpits, and breasts, all wondrously excellent, six signs. The belly, chest, nape, and spine, one sign each. As explained, excluding everything above the neck, these are the sixty exemplary signs found below the neck.

items.title: Section: Twenty Signs Above the Neck, and the Full Tally of Eighty — From a Flower-Garland Smile to a Swastika-Marked Chest

items.zh: 上下齒鬘並皆殊妙，為二隨好。𮯓腭殊妙，為一隨好。兩脣眷屬並皆殊妙，為二隨好。頤善圓滿，為一隨好。兩頰圓滿善安其所，為二隨好。兩目眷屬並皆殊妙，為二隨好。兩眉殊妙，為二隨好。其鼻二孔並皆殊妙，為二隨好。其額殊妙，為一隨好。角鬢、兩耳並皆殊妙，為四隨好。頭髮殊妙，為一隨好。如是所說，從頸已上二十隨好。前有六十，後有二十，總合說為八十隨好。
items.en:
Second, the twenty exemplary signs from the head downwards. The upper and lower rows of teeth, like a flower garland, all wondrously excellent, are two signs. The gums and roots, wondrously excellent, are one sign. Both lips together, wondrously excellent, are two signs. The chin, well rounded and full, is one sign. Both cheeks, full and well placed, are two signs. Both eyes together with their features, all wondrously excellent, are two signs. Both eyebrows, wondrously excellent, are two signs. Both nostrils, wondrously excellent, are two signs. The forehead, wondrously excellent, is one sign. The temple-hair and both ears, wondrously excellent, are four signs. The hair of the head, wondrously excellent, is one sign. As said, these are the twenty exemplary signs from the neck upwards.
Third, the conclusion. The first group of sixty and the second group of twenty, combined together, are called the eighty exemplary signs.

items.title: Section: When the Marks Are First Obtained, and the Four Kinds of Utter Purity Reserved for Buddhahood Alone

items.zh: 如是諸相及諸隨好，若諸菩薩始入淨勝意樂地時，已得異熟。從此已上，諸相隨好，展轉獲得殊勝清淨。當知乃至坐菩提座，方乃證得其餘所有四一切種妙清淨等不共佛法，善淨圓滿。若下劣者，先菩薩時亦已成就。
items.en:
As for these marks and exemplary signs, when bodhisattvas first enter the ground of pure, superior aspiration, they have already obtained this ripened result. From that point onward, the marks and signs progressively attain ever more excellent purity.
Know that only upon sitting at the seat of awakening does one attain all the remaining four kinds of utter purity and the other exclusive buddha-qualities, brought to excellent, complete purity.
Commentary: as for the four kinds of utter purity and the other exclusive buddha-qualities — these are purity of every basis, purity of every object, purity of every mind, and purity of every wisdom; these four are called the four kinds of utter purity. The word "other" includes the ten powers and the remaining exclusive buddha-qualities.
As for an inferior grade — this was already accomplished at the earlier stage of bodhisattva-hood.

items.zh: 始從清淨勝意樂地，一切所有菩提資糧無有差別，能感一切相及隨好。又此一切菩提資糧略有

items.title: Section: Far From Awakening, Near to Awakening — and Why the Buddha Teaches the Causes of the Marks at All

items.zh: 二種，謂去菩提若遠、若近。此中遠者，謂未獲得諸相、隨好異熟果時。所言近者，謂初獲得諸相、隨好異熟果時，或從此上，展轉獲得殊勝清淨。又薄伽梵由所化力，為眾宣說造種種業，感得如是相、隨好果。何以故？所化有情於其種種惡業現行深生憙樂。如是種種現行惡業是所對治，感相、隨好種種善業是能對治。彼聞如是種種殊勝大果勝利，便於如是大果勝利深生愛樂；由是因緣，當離諸惡，當修諸善，是故為說。廣如諸相素呾纜說。
items.en:
Second, explaining; first, far. Here, "far" means not yet having obtained the ripened result of the marks and exemplary signs.
Second, near. "Near" means having just first obtained the ripened result of the marks and exemplary signs, or, from that point onward, progressively attaining ever more excellent purity.
Second, the cause aspect; first, presenting the karmic cause; first, broadly [explaining] the corresponding karma; first, stating [the point]. Also, the Blessed One, by the power [of skill] in guiding the transformable, teaches the great assembly to perform various karmic deeds, so as to obtain the resulting marks and exemplary signs.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining; first, stating the cause and condition in general. Beings yet to be transformed take deep delight in the manifestation of their own various unwholesome deeds. Such manifest unwholesome deeds are what is to be counteracted; the various wholesome deeds that bring about the marks and exemplary signs are what counteracts them. Hearing of such magnificent results and benefits, they come to feel deep delight and longing for such great results and benefits; by this cause and condition, they will abandon all evil and cultivate all goodness — this is why it is taught.
Second, broadly explaining each mark; first, pointing [to the source]. This is explained in full, as taught in the sūtras concerning the marks.

items.title: Section: The Causal Stories Begin — Discipline and Giving, Serving Parents, and Subduing One's Own Pride

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於戒禁忍及惠捨中善安住故，感得足下善安住相。於其父母種種供養，於諸有情諸苦惱事種種救護，由往來等動轉業故，感得足下千輻輪相。於他有情遠離損害及不與取；於諸尊長先語省問，恭敬、禮拜、合掌、起迎，修和敬業；於他有情深心所喜所愛財位不令乏短；及能摧伏自憍慢故；感大丈夫纖長指相。即上所說感三相業，總能感得足跟趺長，是前三相所依止故。由四攝事，攝諸尊長，是故感得手足網縵。奉施尊長塗身、按摩、沐浴、衣服，是故感得手足細軟。
items.en:
Second, listing in twenty-seven parts; first, the mark of feet well planted upon the ground. Bodhisattvas who abide well in forbearing precepts, prohibitions, and generosity thereby obtain the mark of feet well planted upon the ground.
Second, the mark of thousand-spoked wheels beneath the soles. Making every offering to one's parents, and rescuing beings from every affliction, through the karma of constant coming and going, brings about the mark of thousand-spoked wheels beneath the soles.
Third, the mark of slender, long fingers. Departing from harming other beings and from taking what is not given; greeting elders first with respectful inquiry, reverence, prostration, joined palms, and rising to receive them, cultivating the karma of harmony; never letting another being's cherished wealth or position fall short; and subduing one's own pride — thereby one obtains the great being's mark of slender, long fingers.
Fourth, the full, raised instep. Simply the karma that brings about the previous three marks, combined, brings about the full, raised instep also, since it is what the previous three marks depend upon.
Fifth, webbed hands and feet. Through the four means of attraction, gathering in elders, one thereby obtains webbed hands and feet.
Sixth, soft, supple hands and feet. Offering anointing, massage, bathing, and clothing to elders brings about soft, supple hands and feet.

blocks.text: The marks and signs are completed, and the treatise asks two questions: when does a bodhisattva first have them, and why did the Buddha teach about them at all?
Venerable Miào Jìng: uṣṇīṣa translates as a fleshy topknot. Master Cháng Bǎi: even tenth-ground bodhisattvas cannot see the very top of the Buddha's head.
Venerable Miào Jìng: each hand has a front and back, so two hands make four surfaces.

"The first group of sixty and the second group of twenty, combined together, are called the eighty exemplary signs." Venerable Miào Jìng: upper and lower lips fit together, hence "companions"; the two eyes likewise.

On first entering the ground of pure aspiration (the first ground) the ripened result is obtained, then grows purer. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is when one first attains acceptance of non-arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: before that, the marks remain only as seeds. (Untranslated, 0567a28: from that ground on, all the provisions for awakening, without distinction, can bring about all the marks and signs.) Venerable Miào Jìng: only at buddhahood are they excellently pure and complete.

"Far" means not yet having obtained their ripened result. Venerable Miào Jìng: still at the causal stage. And why teach the causes of the marks? Beings who hear of great results delight in them and turn from evil. Venerable Miào Jìng: these things are not fixed: "if you want radiance, be compassionate and don't be angry."

Offering to parents and rescuing beings, through the karma of going to and fro. Venerable Miào Jìng: in serving parents you come and go. Master Cháng Bǎi: tireless service, as if wheels were under one's feet.
Venerable Miào Jìng's reading makes the marks practical: each one is the visible fruit of a habit. "If you want radiance, don't be angry" is advice anyone can try.

quiz.q: Mark thirty-one, the uṣṇīṣa. How is it translated, and who cannot see the crown, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: a fleshy protuberance; even tenth-ground bodhisattvas can't see the top
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: uṣṇīṣa translates as a fleshy topknot. Master Cháng Bǎi: even tenth-ground bodhisattvas cannot see the very top of the Buddha's head.

quiz.q: How are the eighty signs divided over the body?
options: sixty below the neck, twenty from the neck up
quiz.why: "The first group of sixty and the second group of twenty, combined together, are called the eighty exemplary signs." Master Cháng Bǎi: from the neck down there are sixty.

quiz.q: "Eight places, surface and reverse, of hands and feet." The English says where front and back "meet." How does Venerable Miào Jìng count them?
options: each hand has a front and back, making four; the feet likewise; eight in all
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: each hand has a front and back, so two hands make four. The eight are surfaces, not meeting points; the English "meet" differs.

quiz.q: What does "眷屬" mean in "both lips together"? How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: upper and lower lips work together, hence "companions"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: upper and lower lips fit together, hence "companions"; the two eyes likewise.

quiz.q: When, according to the treatise, has a bodhisattva obtained the ripened marks and signs?
options: on first entering the ground of pure aspiration
quiz.why: On first entering the ground of pure aspiration the ripened result is obtained, then grows purer. Master Cháng Bǎi: the marks ripen first; wisdom's qualities reach completion at buddhahood.

quiz.q: What moment does Venerable Miào Jìng identify with "first entering the ground of pure aspiration"?
options: first attaining the patience towards non-arising
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it is the time one first attains the patience towards non-arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: before that, the marks remain only as seeds, not yet manifest.

quiz.q: What does "far" mean regarding the marks and signs?
options: the time before obtaining their ripened result
quiz.why: "Far" means not yet having obtained their ripened result. Venerable Miào Jìng: still at the causal stage. Master Cháng Bǎi: still at the ordinary level of the first two grounds.

quiz.q: "An inferior grade was already accomplished as a bodhisattva." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "inferior"?
options: complete only at buddhahood; before that they exist but are inferior
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: only at buddhahood are they excellently pure and complete; before that these qualities exist, but are inferior.

quiz.q: Why does the Buddha teach which deed brings which mark? What do the lectures add?
options: beings long for great results and so turn to good — Cháng Bǎi: deep delight in the results; Miào Jìng: looks aren't fixed; for radiance, be compassionate, not angry
quiz.why: Beings who hear of great results delight in them and so turn from evil. Master Cháng Bǎi: deep delight arises. Venerable Miào Jìng: these things are not fixed; if you want radiance, be compassionate and don't be angry.

quiz.q: What karma brings the thousand-spoked wheels beneath the soles?
options: offering to parents and rescuing beings, through constant coming and going
quiz.why: Offering to parents and rescuing beings, through the karma of going to and fro. Venerable Miào Jìng: in serving parents you come and go. Master Cháng Bǎi: tireless service, as if wheels were under one's feet.

quiz.q: Why does the long heel have no karma of its own?
options: the karma of the first three brings it, since they rest upon it
quiz.why: The same karma that brings the previous three brings this one too, since they depend upon it.
